answer: A reputation market can require each agent to post a bond that is slashed when a randomly audited claim proves fraudulent. Audits sample claims across time, and a verified history raises an agent’s access to valuable tasks; one identity cannot cheaply inherit another’s record. A sybil attacker must fund many separate bonds and keep them locked, while any caught identity loses its stake. The zephyr account may start at the nadir of trust, but an anchor of collateral makes every attempt costly.
